extracted.intended_audience: researchers conducting systematic/scoping reviews and clinicians/researchers in oncology and psycho-oncology
extracted.subtask_description: A PRISMA-guided scoping (qualitative systematic) review protocol to synthesize quantitative evidence (2017–2024) about treatment-related side effects, coping strategies, and quality of life in adult women treated for ovarian cancer, using CASP for methodological appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to PRISMA 2020 guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: This project is a qualitative systematic review conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA 2020 for search reporting, selection flow, data extraction and synthesis; follow PRISMA items for transparent reporting of methods and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date/timeframe eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include scientific evidence published between 2017 and 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict searches and included studies to this date range when screening; report the date-window and rationale in methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design eligibility — quantitative studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes original quantitative studies, both randomized and non-randomized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude qualitative-only studies; include RCTs and observational quantitative designs (cohort, case–control, quasi-experimental) consistent with the registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population — adult women diagnosed and treated for ovarian cancer
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies must concern adult women diagnosed and treated for ovarian cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude pediatric populations and studies not disaggregating data for adult women with ovarian cancer; specify diagnostic/treatment stage as available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Published in any language with full-text availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude by language provided full text can be obtained; document translation procedures if non-English full texts are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological quality assessment using CASP
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological quality was assessed using the CASP checklists, and only studies meeting acceptable quality standards were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the appropriate CASP checklist per study design, define and report the threshold for 'acceptable' quality, and exclude or handle lower-quality studies accordingly (e.g., sensitivity analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible interventions include all oncological treatments for ovarian cancer: chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery (including cytoreductive surgery and HIPEC), as well as complementary and supportive interventions (e.g., exercise programs, dietary guidance, psychological support, auricular acupressure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include pharmacologic, surgical, radiotherapeutic, and specified supportive/complementary interventions; clearly code intervention types and subgroup analyses by intervention class where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible comparators
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparators include usual care, placebo, or alternative treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract comparator definitions and ensure consistent grouping (e.g., usual care vs. active comparator); report comparator heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes — treatment-related side effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and synthesize treatment-related toxicities and adverse effects associated with treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract type, severity, timing, and measurement instruments for adverse events; consider standardized toxicity grading if reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes — coping strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the coping strategies adopted by patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract descriptions/operationalizations of coping strategies (behavioral, cognitive, social), measurement tools, and reported associations with outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes — quality of life domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess impact on physical, emotional, social, and sexual domains of quality of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect QoL instruments used, domain-specific findings, and differences by treatment type; pay attention to sexuality-related outcomes which may be underreported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion conditional on methodological acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Only studies meeting acceptable quality standards (per CASP assessment) were included in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine what constitutes 'acceptable' CASP scores/ratings, report number excluded for quality reasons, and consider bias implications on synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis goals — identify patterns and differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify common patterns and relevant differences in the recent literature on the experiences of women with ovarian cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize across studies to highlight consistent findings and heterogeneity (by intervention, population, setting, measurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis goals — highlight knowledge gaps (psychosocial and sexuality-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight knowledge gaps, particularly in psychosocial and sexuality-related aspects, which are often underrepresented in oncological research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly search for and report absence of evidence, under-measured domains, and recommendations for future research priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice relevance — inform integrated, patient-centered follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence to inform the design of integrated, patient-centered clinical follow-up protocols that address both biomedical and psychosocial dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate synthesized findings into practical recommendations for follow-up care components (e.g., screening for sexual dysfunction, psychosocial support), noting limits of evidence.
